How calls are placed, and common questions
Choose something on the left to open it here.
Changing this switches the whole app immediately. The system phone app and system dialogs are not affected.
Numbers stored without a country code get this one added when they are dialled. A number that already starts with + is left exactly as it is.

Short service numbers such as 110 or 10086 are dialled as they are, with no code added. A number written with a leading 0 - a landline, say 01012345678 - is dialled as +86 10 1234 5678: the 0 belongs to the old country, and the dialling code replaces it.

If the phone has two SIM cards, the system asks which one to use. A family member can set a default SIM in the phone\'s own settings.
You can grant it again, or turn it on in the system settings. Press the Call button again afterwards.
Answering, cancelling, hanging up and speakerphone all happen in the system phone app, which this app cannot control.

1. A family member adds the photo and number under "Manage contacts".
2. The elderly user opens the app and sees the photos.
3. Press the green Call button under a photo.
4. Cancel or hang up in the system phone app.
Version, GitHub project, update check and privacy
This asks GitHub for the newest version number. Nothing else is sent, and the app works the same without a connection.
You already have the newest version.
No version has been published for download yet.
Could not read the newest version from GitHub. Check the connection and try again.
No app on this phone can open web pages. The address is %1$s
The contacts, photos and settings you add stay on this phone, in this app\'s own storage. Nothing is uploaded to a server, and there is no account and no login.
There are no ads, no usage statistics and no crash reports.
The only network request this app can make is the update check above, and only when it is tapped. It asks GitHub for the newest version number and sends no name, number or photo.
Calls are placed by the phone app, not by this app. The contacts permission is read-only and is used only when a family member imports people from the address book.
An exported file contains names, phone numbers and photos, and it is not encrypted. Send it only to people you trust.
